newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-LINESMAN ATTACKED AFTER LATE GOAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LINESMAN ATTACKED AFTER LATE GOAL.

text.p: A linesman was attacked by livid soccer players after a controversial late goal on Sunday in the latest violence to hit Brazil's soccer pitches.
Play was delayed for 15 minutes as violence erupted on the field in the Rio de Janeiro championship match between Madureira and Flamengo.

The linesman and match referee Jorge Rabello both needed police to protect them from Madureira players and officials, who were furious at seeing their modest team denied a famous shock win over giants Flamengo.
Madureira, a small club from a distant Rio de Janeiro suburb, were leading 1-0 at home to Flamengo, Brazil's best supported club, until injury time.
But in their last attack, Flamengo, whose team includes Brazilian World Cup hero Romario, equalised through substitute Marco Aurelio.

Marco Aurelio's shot hit the Madureira woodwork, bounced down and back into play. The referee originally disallowed the goal, waving play on, but changed his mind after the linesman signalled the ball had crossed the line.

Madureira players rushed towards the linesman, who was saved when several police dived in to protect him. Players then pushed and shoved police and Madureira's reserve goalkeeper was seen being wrestled to the ground by one officer.

Meanwhile, dozens of people, including club officials, security men, hangers-on and journalists, ran onto the field. As usual in Brazilian matches, it was impossible to identify who was who in the melee.

After around ten minutes, police formed a huge cordon to allow the referee back onto the field. But as soon as he reached the centre circle, Madureira players ran towards him and began arguing, club officials joined in and the whole storm blew up again.

One man, identified as the Madureira president, led the protests. On being told by a reporter that television replays had showed Flamengo's goal to be legitimate, the man shouted: "That's because you're all Flamengo."
After 15 minutes, play was able to restart. Less than one minute was played before the referee blew for time.
Replays clearly showed the ball had crossed the line before hitting a net support behind the crossbar and then bouncing down and hitting the ground in front of the goal line.
Romario, who steered clear of the mayhem, said: "This is yet another lamentable incident in our football."
In the first stage of the competition, Flamengo had beaten Madureira 7-0 in a match which also ended with a brawl.

Several other games in the tournament have also been interrupted by fights. In one match, the coach of Itaperuna ran on to the field, ripped off his shirt and dropped his trousers because, he said, his team was being robbed.
On Thursday, Valtenir, goalkeeper of Rio Branco-Acre, was taken to a police station and charged with assault after attacking a referee who sent him off in a Copa Brasil game against Flamengo.
Botafogo, who won the first stage of the Rio de Janeiro championship, lead the second stage after beating Volta Redonda 2-1 away. The winners of each of the first three stages qualify for a play-off.
Palmeiras and Corinthians both won in the Sao Paulo championship to stay clear leaders of their respective groups. Palmeiras beat Mogi Mirim 2-0 and Corinthians thrashed America 5-0.
